results.title: Opinion: Compulsion Loops In The Short, Medium and Long-term
excerpts: # Opinion: Compulsion Loops In The Short, Medium and Long-term In this reprinted opinion piece, Hogrocket co-founder and creative director Pete Collier explains why games should have three compulsion loops to keep players engaged. December 28, 2011 7 Min Read Game Developer logo in a gray background | Game Developer [](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](http://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](http://www.twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.gamedeveloper. com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term&title=Opinion%3A%20Compulsion%20Loops%20In%20The%20Short%2C%20Medium%20and%20Long-term) [](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Opinion%3A%20Compulsion%20Loops%20In%20The%20Short%2C%20Medium%20and%20Long-term%20-%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gamedeveloper.com%2Fdesign%2Fopinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) Author: by Pete Collier [In this reprinted [\#altdevblogaday](http://altdevblogaday.com/) opinion piece, Hogrocket co-founder and creative director Pete Collier [explains why games should have three compulsion loops](http://www.petecollier.com/) to keep players engaged.] Compulsion loop is a very fancy term isn't it? It's a recently coined term, perhaps a couple of years old, I'm unsure of its exact origin. However, there is no official definition of it, so as a result it's often bandied around with slight nervousness lest someone asks you what it actually is. This of course is the point at which you run away screaming, mumbling crazily something about [Zynga](http://www.zynga.com) and the horrors of manipulation, death and pestilence or whatever. My definition of a compulsion loop is that it is a construct designed to keep someone engaged by marrying their action/s with an appropriate level of reward. But in essence it has been around forever, we just didn't have a name for it. Compulsion loops in the short, medium and long-term, if visualized, would resemble helm chain The greatest creators of entertainment have had an innate understanding of it since we all sat around the fire scratching our heads as Neanderthals. It's nothing new. Different mediums achieve it in their own way, but all essentially reward for attention and effort and when this equilibrium falters the loop dissipates. Here is the rub though; reward for effort in the short-term is very different to what we want in the long-term. Whack-a-mole forever would be hell on earth right? At some point we want a deeper sense of reward from an activity beyond the short-term thrills and if we don't get it, we move on. It is diminishing returns. So we need to examine what keeps people compelled beyond the here and now. To this end I believe there needs to be three compulsion loops engaging us at the same time, tapping into our desire for different kinds of gratification in the short, medium and long-term. The most compelling experiences keep on giving through all these timeframes allowing people to form a deep and lasting attachment, which is of course a quality that society and all of us individually cherish in an experience. So how do we aim to achieve this with our games? To answer this, I think we need to look at what drives us in each of these timeframes, then ask how that can help inform the way we structure our games. ... Our lives are now crammed with many opportunities promising instant reward and yes many of them are false and empty, but their potential for distraction is very real. You could indeed argue many people are permanently distracted by this chase (I'm looking at you western culture). Now more than ever your game needs to give compelling reasons for the player to return. This needs to involve long-term attachment because short-term compulsion has such a weak hold, even when done well. A deeper hook is needed to keep the player caught. The transition point between the short and long-term is therefore a critical juncture. The fragile attachment developed by players in the short-term can easily shatter and curiosity wane. That deeper hook needs to be alluded to in the medium-term by giving context to the player's actions. Framing short-term activity as building blocks contributing toward a greater structure should be a key goal for the designer. It is the job of compulsion loops in the medium-term to convert the player from folly and a dazed state of preoccupation to a sense of clear purpose. Action needs to be rewarded with a sense of contribution toward something, rather than being disparate, unconnected and meaningless. If you still have the player in the medium-term you are affording more leeway with your compulsion loops but it is crucial that they are leveraged as much as possible. The medium-term is about deferred gratification because the action here is not about offering a direct reward but the promise of a greater one if you continue building. Frame the contribution toward a greater structure... Long-term: Legacy And Reflective Gratification As in life, players want their short and medium term activities to amount to something in the long-term. We all seek meaning, if the short-term can be the worst of us; the long-term can be the most noble in our pursuit of it. ... Long-term compulsion loops then, are afforded the greatest size but it is imperative that the structure reflects accomplishment, allows for demonstration of mastery and serves as a meaningful embodiment of the player's journey. In an ironic final twist the long-term compulsion loop is but a mere apparition. It never fulfills its loop, but it doesn't matter. What does the player leave behind? Conclusion: We are compelled to draw more from life, as we are in a game, the more we're engaged by it. It is our conviction of purpose in the short and medium-term that ultimately justify our achievements in the long-term and keep us motivated to keep pushing forward. It's when we lose this that things stagnate and we seek change. Compulsion loops are often cited as the worst of game development, that it is somehow bringing too much science and manipulation into the art of making games. In my opinion it is actually the opposite and quite beautiful. It lies at the very beating heart of human nature and what we want from our experiences. I say, what better way is there, in fact, to frame how we should approach the way in which we make our games? This article was originally posted on my blog: [Compulsion Loops in the Short, Medium and Long-term](http://www.petecollier.com) [This piece was reprinted from [\#AltDevBlogADay](http://altdevblogaday.com/) , a shared blog initiative started by [@mike\_acton](http://www.twitter.com/mike_acton) devoted to giving game developers of all disciplines a place to motivate each other to write regularly about their personal game development passions.] [](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](http://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](http://www.twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www. gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) [](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/opinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term&title=Opinion%3A%20Compulsion%20Loops%20In%20The%20Short%2C%20Medium%20and%20Long-term) [](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Opinion%3A%20Compulsion%20Loops%20In%20The%20Short%2C%20Medium%20and%20Long-term%20-%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gamedeveloper.com%2Fdesign%2Fopinion-compulsion-loops-in-the-short-medium-and-long-term) Daily news, dev blogs, and stories from Game Developer straight to your inbox [Stay Updated](https://gd-resources.gamedeveloper.com/free/w_gamf01/prgm.cgi) ### Latest News More News The Godot logo on a blue background Business Godot to ban (almost all) AI coding contributions Godot to ban (almost all) AI coding contributions by Diego Argüello Jul 1, 2026 2 Min Read

results.title: How Game Designers Use Feedback Loops to Keep ... - Medium
excerpts:
Each reward reinforces desired behavior and motivates the player to continue engaging with the game.

Additionally, feedback loops exploit the concept of **variable rewards** , where players receive unpredictable yet appealing incentives. This unpredictability can create a compelling sense of anticipation, much like a slot machine, which encourages prolonged engagement. Many mobile and social games rely heavily on variable rewards to maximize playtime and retention.

## Types of Feedback Loops in Games

Game designers employ several types of feedback loops to keep players hooked:

1. **Progression Loops** : These loops revolve around the player’s advancement in the game. For example, leveling up a character, unlocking new abilities, or gaining access to more challenging missions all provide immediate and long-term satisfaction. The sense of progression acts as a continual motivator, encouraging players to invest more time and effort.
2.
**Skill Feedback Loops** : Games that emphasize skill improvement often reward players for mastery. Achievements, leaderboards, and ranking systems provide clear indicators of skill progression. When players see measurable improvement, they are motivated to refine their abilities further.
3. **Resource Loops** : In strategy or simulation games, resources such as money, materials, or energy are collected and spent in cycles. These loops encourage players to plan and optimize, making decisions that affect both short-term and long-term gameplay outcomes.
4. **Social Feedback Loops** : Multiplayer and online games leverage social interaction as a feedback mechanism. Players gain recognition, rewards, or status from their peers, which strengthens community ties and encourages continuous participation. Social loops can be particularly effective because they combine intrinsic motivation with extrinsic rewards.

results.title: Action → Feedback → Reward → Motivation → Repeat: The Compulsive Game Loop That Hooks You | by Algoryte | Medium
excerpts:
This is what players spend the majority of their time doing. The core loop must be immediately satisfying because players will experience it hundreds or thousands of times.

In _Call of Duty_ , the core loop is: spawn → navigate → engage enemies → eliminate/die → respawn.

In _Stardew Valley_ , it’s: plant crops → water → harvest → sell → buy seeds.

### **Meta Loop (Long-term Progression)**

The meta loop operates on a much larger scale, typically spanning hours or entire play sessions. It provides long-term motivation and a sense of progression beyond individual actions. Live service games often use seasonal meta loops where players work toward battle pass rewards or ranked progression over weeks or months.

In RPG making, this might be: complete quests → level up → unlock new abilities → access new areas → face tougher challenges.

### **Micro Loop (Moment-to-Moment Actions)**

...

* **Use Analytics to Track Loop Completion:** Instrument your game to measure completion rates, stuck points, and phase timing to reveal problems that aren’t obvious during development and make informed design decisions rather than guessing.
* **Don’t Add Complexity Before Mastering Simplicity:** Master a simple, tight loop first and only add new mechanics when the existing loop feels completely polished.
* **Study Games You Find Addictive:** Whenever you catch yourself saying “just one more,” analyze what loop is driving that compulsion by breaking down the cycle of actions and understanding why you’re motivated to repeat it.
* **Balance Instant and Delayed Gratification:** Layer short-term rewards (responsive controls, clear feedback, quick rewards) with long-term goals (meaningful progression, unlockable content, narrative payoff) so there’s always something to work toward at multiple timescales.

results.title: game-designer/guides/game-mechanics-engagement-loops-player-psychology.md at main · AlexWynn-AM/game-designer · GitHub
excerpts:
They provide direction and purpose to the short loops.

| Genre | Long Loop Example |
|-------|-------------------|
| Combat RPG | Clear a dungeon floor, defeat a boss, complete a quest chain |
| Tycoon | Unlock the next tier of machines, reach a revenue milestone |
| Horror | Survive an entire floor, unlock a new area |
| Social/Roleplay | Complete a house renovation, trade for a desired pet |

**Design principle**: Long loops should have a **clear endpoint** that the player can visualize and work toward. "I need 500 more coins to buy the next sword" is a compelling session goal.

#### Meta Loops (Progression/Retention) -- Days to Months

Meta loops are what keep players returning over weeks and months. They operate above individual sessions and encompass the player's total journey.

| System | Meta Loop Example |
|--------|-------------------|
| Prestige/Rebirth | Reset progress with permanent multipliers, climb again faster |
| Seasonal Content | Limited-time events, battle passes, exclusive rewards |
| Collection Completion | Fill out a bestiary, collect all fruits, unlock all achievements |
| Social Investment | Guild progression, friend networks, trade reputation |
| Skill Mastery | PvP ranking, leaderboard climbing, speedrun optimization |

**Design principle**: While short loops keep a player engaged for 5 minutes, the meta loop keeps them playing for 5 months. The meta loop introduces long-term progression systems, replay incentives, and resource management to deepen player investment.

### 1.4 Examples from Top Roblox Games

#### Blox Fruits

**Genre**: Action RPG / MMO (One Piece-inspired)

**Core Loop**: Explore -> Fight -> Loot -> Upgrade -> Explore Further

- **Short loop**: Find enemies -> Use fruit abilities + fighting styles in combat -> Defeat enemies -> Collect XP and drops
- **Long loop**: Level up to access the next island, obtain a new Devil Fruit, unlock a new fighting style
- **Meta loop**: Progress through First Sea -> Second Sea -> Third Sea, prestige fighting styles, collect all fruits, PvP ranking

**What makes it work**:
- Early gameplay is intuitive while mastery is earned over time
- Four combat pillars (Devil Fruits, Fighting Styles, Swords, Guns) offer build variety
- All content is free to access; monetization is through time-saving tools (2x XP, faster boats)
- Fruits spawn randomly every 45-60 minutes, creating natural return incentives
- Three seas create a clear macro-progression path with escalating power and complexity
- Fighting styles are color-coded by rarity/progression stage: Green (First Sea), Blue (Second Sea), Red (Third Sea)

#### Adopt Me!

**Genre**: Pet Economy / Social Roleplay

**Core Loop**: Nurture Pets -> Complete Tasks -> Earn Currency -> Trade/Collect -> Nurture More

- **Short loop**: Feed pet, play mini-games, complete daily tasks
- **Long loop**: Age up a pet to full-grown, trade for a desired pet, design/decorate home

...

- **Meta loop**: Progress through worlds, complete collection, trade for ultra-rare pets, unlock all areas

**What makes it work**:
- Layered reward loops (active tapping + passive idle gains) broaden audience
- Pet rarity system (Golden, Rainbow, Shiny variants) adds excitement to every hatch
- Merging mechanics (3 identical pets -> 1 pet with 2x power) provide a satisfying resource sink
- Idle income means the game rewards players even when offline
- Trading ecosystem keeps players logging in not just to play but to trade

#### Tower of Hell

**Genre**: Skill-based Obby / Competitive Platformer

**Core Loop**: Attempt Tower -> Climb Stages -> Reach Top or Fall -> Retry with New Tower

- **Short loop**: Jump, dodge obstacles, navigate platforms under time pressure
- **Long loop**: Successfully complete a randomly generated tower, beat personal best times
- **Meta loop**: Skill improvement over time, cosmetic unlocks, leaderboard competition

**What makes it work**:

...

#### Socializers (Hearts) -- "Interact with Players"
- **Motivation**: Building relationships, communicating, collaborating with other players
- **Behaviors**: Chatting, forming groups, helping newbies, roleplaying, organizing events
- **Roblox design hooks**: Trading systems, co-op mechanics, guilds/groups, social spaces, house decoration (visible to others), chat systems
- **Example**: An Adopt Me! player who spends most time trading pets and decorating their home for friends to visit

#### Killers (Clubs) -- "Act on Players"
- **Motivation**: Competing against and imposing on other players, demonstrating dominance
- **Behaviors**: PvP combat, griefing (in extreme cases), dominating leaderboards, competitive play
- **Roblox design hooks**: PvP arenas, ranked matchmaking, kill/death leaderboards, competitive events, bounty systems
- **Example**: A Blox Fruits player focused on PvP combat in the Second/Third Sea

...

- **Retry-friendly design**: Quick respawn, low penalty for failure, easy restart -- keeps players in flow rather than punishing them out of it

### 2.4 Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Motivation

Understanding the interplay between these two motivation types is essential for designing games that engage immediately AND retain long-term.

#### Intrinsic Motivation -- "I play because it's fun"
Driven by internal satisfaction: curiosity, mastery, creativity, social connection, self-expression.

**Examples in games:**
- The satisfaction of nailing a difficult platforming sequence (Tower of Hell)
- The joy of discovering a hidden room or secret (Doors)
- The creative expression of building and decorating (Brookhaven, Adopt Me!)
- The social pleasure of trading and collaborating (Adopt Me!, TDS)

#### Extrinsic Motivation -- "I play for the reward"
Driven by external outcomes: points, badges, currency, cosmetics, rankings, avoiding loss.

**Examples in games:**

...

- **Engagement-Based Payouts**: Developers are paid based on how much time Premium subscribers spend in their game.
- **DevEx (Developer Exchange)**: Creators can convert earned Robux to real money at a rate of $0.0038 USD per Robux.

**Monetization philosophy of top games**: Revenue models integrate cosmetics, time-saving conveniences, and event-driven purchases rather than aggressive paywalls. Well-designed economies outperform forced spending.

### 3.4 Prestige/Rebirth Mechanics

Prestige (also called rebirth, ascension, reincarnation, or New Game+) is a mechanic where players voluntarily reset some or all progress in exchange for permanent bonuses that persist across future runs.

#### How Prestige Works

```
FIRST RUN:        Level 1 -----> Level 100 (Prestige available)
                                      |
                                      v (Reset)
SECOND RUN:        Level 1 -----> Level 100 (Faster due to bonuses)
  + 2x XP bonus                       |
THIRD RUN:         Level 1 -----> Level 100 (Even faster)
  + 4x XP bonus
  + More prestige currency
  + Exclusive unlocks
```

#### Design Purposes

1. **Manages number inflation**: Resets bring growth back to manageable levels, giving developers a stable number to base upgrades on
2. **Creates the "power fantasy" loop**: Starting over with massive bonuses gives a sense of overwhelming power
3. **Extends content lifespan**: The same content provides new experiences at different prestige levels
4. **Enables aspirational goals**: Prestige-exclusive content motivates long-term play
5. **Compresses cognitive load**: Players re-learn systems with deeper understanding each cycle

#### Layered Prestige

Many successful idle/incremental games implement multiple prestige layers:
- **Layer 1**: Reset levels, gain prestige points for permanent stat boosts
- **Layer 2**: Reset levels AND prestige points, gain "ascension tokens" for even more powerful bonuses
- **Layer 3**: Reset everything below, gain "transcendence currency" for game-changing abilities

Each layer resets all layers below it, creating nested loops of investment and return.

#### Roblox Examples

- **Blox Fruits**: While not a traditional prestige system, the Sea progression (First -> Second -> Third) functions similarly, with players needing to reach level thresholds to progress to fundamentally new areas with stronger enemies, better fruits, and advanced fighting styles
- **Pet Simulator 99**: Multiple world progressions function as soft prestige, with each new world requiring re-investment in area progression while keeping permanent pet collection
- **Tycoon games**: Many Roblox tycoons offer rebirth mechanics where players reset their factory/business for permanent production multipliers

### 3.5 Daily Rewards and Login Streaks

Daily reward systems leverage **operant conditioning** to create habit loops:

```

...

**Retroactive credit**: If possible, award badges for things players already did
3. **Visible progress**: Show "47/50 enemies defeated" not just the requirement
4. **Exclusive cosmetics**: Tie rare badges to visual rewards others can see
5. **Don't overwhelm**: A focused set of meaningful achievements beats hundreds of trivial ones

### 3.7 Quest/Mission Systems

Quests provide **directed purpose** within the core loop, transforming open-ended gameplay into goal-oriented sessions.
